narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 68% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. That is a high-risk estimate, not a certainty: it means the review treated your application as too risky to advance.

The strongest factor behind this prediction was your third-year class rank. You were in the second decile, well below the average of about the sixth decile among accepted students. This was the most influential feature and it pushed the prediction toward failure. The second most influential factor was your Law School Admission Test score. Your score of 40 is above the accepted-student average of about 37, so this factor pushed toward passing, but it was not strong enough to outweigh the concern about your third-year rank. Your first-year rank, fifth decile versus an accepted average near sixth, was the third most influential factor and also pushed modestly toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.0 was slightly below the accepted average of 3.23, though it was not among the top drivers.

To improve future chances, focus on the clearest area of concern: your recent academic performance. Consider additional coursework or a post-baccalaureate record that demonstrates stronger grades, seek academic advising, and explain your circumstances in any future application. You may also consider retaking the LSAT if you can meaningfully raise your score, and apply to programs that review candidates holistically.
